Creates a base plane along a main axis. brep only — it needs the kernel's notion of
a workplane, which meshup does not have.

entries.name: box
entries.sig: (width?: number, depth?: number, height?: number, position?: PointLike): Mesh
entries.doc:
Make a box. Only the width given makes a cube. The box starts centred on the
origin; move it into place with move(), moveTo() or align().

params.name: width
params.doc: Size along x

params.name: depth
params.doc: Size along y; the width when left out

params.name: height

params.doc: How far to move it from the origin, as `[x, y, z]`

entries.name: boxBetween
entries.doc:
Make a box with two opposite corners at the given points. Handy when you know
where a part starts and ends rather than its size.

params.name: from
params.doc: One corner

params.name: to
params.doc: The opposite corner

examples: boxBetween([0, 0, 0], [60, 60, 720])   // a table leg standing on the ground

entries.name: circle
entries.doc: Make a circle outline, flat on the ground.

params.name: radius
params.doc: Radius of the circle

params.name: center
params.doc: Where the middle of the circle goes

entries.name: collection
entries.doc:
Create a ShapeCollection that only REFERENCES its shapes: the scene graph is left
exactly as it is, so shapes keep the layer they were made in. Safe to build anywhere,
including as a throwaway argument (`make.partList(collection(a,b))`).

Use group() when you also want the shapes gathered under a layer in the scene.
examples:
a = box(100)
b = sphere(60).moveX(200)
collection(a, b).color('green')

entries.name: cone
entries.sig: (bottomRadius?: number, topRadius?: number, height?: number, position?: PointLike): AnyKernelShape
entries.doc: Creates a Cone. brep only — meshup has no cone primitive yet.

entries.name: cylinder
entries.sig: (radius?: number, height?: number, position?: PointLike): Mesh
entries.doc: Make an upright cylinder, centred on the origin.

params.name: radius
params.doc: Radius of the cylinder

params.name: height
params.doc: Height, along z

params.name: position
params.doc: How far to move it from the origin, as `[x, y, z]`

examples: post = cylinder(40, 900).moveZ(450)   // standing on the ground

entries.name: explainIFC
entries.doc:
Print how the model would export to IFC: every product with its IFC entity, PredefinedType and
the evidence for it, as a tree of storeys, elements and their parts. Classification is
automatic, from the scene hierarchy, names and shape proportions. Returns the same text.

entries.name: group
entries.doc:
Create a scene-backed ShapeCollection: a new layer under the current active layer,
with every given Shape MOVED into it - from any layer it was in, because the scene is
a tree and a Shape lives in exactly one place. Shapes added later (`g.add(...)`) are
moved in too.

`group(a, b)` names the layer after the variable it is assigned to (the Runner's
auto-namer); `group('table', a, b)` names it explicitly.

Use collection() when you only want to reference shapes without restructuring.
examples:
top = box(1200, 700, 30).moveZ(735)
leg = box(60, 60, 720)
table = group(top, leg)

entries.name: helix
entries.sig: (radius?: number, height?: number, angle?: number, pivot?: PointLike, direction?: PointLike, lefthand?: boolean, coneSemiAngle?: number): AnyKernelShape
entries.doc: Makes a Helix. brep only — meshup has no helix primitive yet.

entries.name: layer
entries.doc:
Start a layer, or go back to one: the shapes made after it go in that layer. Layers
group shapes in the scene tree, and colour or hide them together.

params.name: name
params.doc: Name of the layer

entries.name: layerShapes
entries.doc: All shapes in the active layer (see layer()).

entries.name: line
entries.doc: Make a straight line between two points.

params.name: start

params.name: end

entries.name: mode
entries.doc: Set Modeler mode: mesh (default) or brep

entries.name: plane
entries.doc:
Make a flat rectangular surface: `plane(width, depth, position, normal)`. Without a
normal it lies flat on the ground; the normal is the direction it faces.

params.name: ...args
params.doc: Width, depth, position of its middle and the direction it faces, in that order; all optional

examples:
plane(200, 100)                            // on the ground
plane(200, 100, [0, 100, 50], [0, 1, 0])   // standing up, facing +y

entries.name: planeBetween

params.name: from

params.name: to

params.name: xp

params.name: y

params.name: z
params.doc: The z coordinate

entries.name: polyline
entries.doc: Make a line with corners: straight segments from point to point.

params.name: points
params.doc: The points in order, as a list or one by one

entries.name: rect

entries.doc: Make a rectangle outline, flat on the ground. Use plane() for a filled rectangle.

params.name: width

params.name: depth
params.doc: Size along y

params.name: center

entries.name: rectBetween

entries.name: select
entries.doc: Select shapes by a selection string — delegates to the active sketch when in sketch mode.

entries.doc:
Start a 2D drawing on a plane: move the pen with moveTo(), draw with lineTo(),
arcTo() and the like, and finish with close() for a closed shape.

params.name: plane
params.doc: The plane to draw on: `'xy'` (the ground), `'xz'` (front) or `'yz'` (side)

entries.name: sphere
entries.doc: Make a ball, centred on the origin.

params.name: radius
params.doc: Radius of the ball

params.name: position
params.doc: Where to put its centre, as `[x, y, z]`

entries.name: spiral
entries.sig: (firstRadius?: number, secondRadius?: number, angle?: number, lefthand?: boolean): AnyKernelShape
entries.doc: Makes a 2D Spiral. brep only — meshup has no spiral primitive yet.

entries.name: spline
entries.doc: Make a smooth curve through a list of points.

params.name: ...points
params.doc: The points the curve passes through, in order

entries.name: units
entries.doc:
Get or set the units the model is built in: all sizes in the script are in these
units. The default is millimetres.
entries.returnsDoc: The units now in use

params.name: u
params.doc: The units to use, such as `'mm'`, `'cm'`, `'m'` or `'inch'`. Leave out to only read them.

examples:
units('cm')
box(100, 60, 4) // a table top of 1 m by 60 cm

entries.name: vector
entries.sig: (xp?: PointLike, y?: number, z?: number): Vector
entries.doc: Make a vector: a direction with a length, for moving and orienting shapes.

params.name: xp

params.name: y
params.doc: The y component

params.name: z
params.doc: The z component

Make a vertex: a point that is part of the model, so it shows in the viewer and

params.name: y
params.doc: The y coordinate

params.name: z
params.doc: The z coordinate

entries.name: $PARAMS
entries.doc:
The parameters of the script. `$PARAMS.define()` adds one; every parameter is
also available as its own global, like `$WIDTH`.

entries.name: calc
entries.doc:
Tables and metrics: numbers and lists that come out of the model, shown in the
Data and Metrics tools and available to configurators.

entries.name: doc
entries.doc: Drawings and documents: pages with views of the model, text, tables and images.

entries.name: docs
entries.doc: Same as `doc`

entries.name: fab
entries.doc: Fabrication: how the parts of the model are cut, joined and priced.

entries.name: make
entries.doc: Ready-made building parts: walls, floors, frames and part lists.

entries.name: materials
entries.doc: Materials to assign to shapes, with their colour, weight and carbon.

entries.name: $component
entries.doc:
Use another script as a component. Returns an importer: set its parameters with
`.params()` and get the shapes with `.get()`. Without a name it lists the scripts
you can use.

params.name: name
params.doc: The script: `'./name'` for one of your own, `'@author/name:version'` for a published one

params.name: params
params.doc: Parameter values for the component, same as `.params()`

entries.name: $handle
entries.doc:
Make a handle: a point in the viewer that users drag to change a parameter.
Place it with `.start(target)` or `.at(target)`.

entries.name: $import
entries.doc:
Import a file from the web (SVG, GeoJSON, DXF, STL, OBJ, glTF, AMF, 3MF) as shapes.
The address must be written out as text, not computed.

params.name: url
params.doc: Web address of the file

params.name: opts
params.doc: Import options, such as scaling and centring

entries.name: $module
entries.doc: Declare a script module (an optional extension installed on the server) and get it.

params.name: name
params.doc: Name of the module, e.g. `'cloudcalc'`

entries.name: $pipeline
entries.doc:
Register a pipeline: a named step that runs after the model, for instance to
prepare shapes for a drawing.

params.name: name
params.doc: Name of the pipeline, referred to by docs and outputs

params.name: fn
params.doc: The function to run

entries.name: exit
entries.doc:
Stop the script here, for instance to look at the model built so far.
The shapes made before it are still shown.

params.name: message
params.doc: Shown with the warning in the console

entries.name: log
entries.doc: Log a message to the console at info level

entries.name: print
entries.doc: Print values to the console, like `console.log()`. Objects are printed as data.

entries.name: mode
entries.doc: Kernel a shape belongs to. meshup shapes are always the mesh kernel.

entries.name: add
entries.doc: Add given Mesh to the current (Alias for union)

entries.name: addAnnotations
entries.doc: Link annotation(s) to this Shape (host-app side of the two-sided annotation link)

entries.name: addToScene
alt: (): this
entries.doc:
Add this shape to the scene, under the active layer of the scene it is bound to.
Clears the sticky `tmp()` flag — `addToScene()` is the documented way back in.

`scene` may be given explicitly (the usual case for a host that owns a root and is
adding a freshly built, never-attached shape); otherwise the shape's own node/carried
root is used. Returns `this` even when no scene is reachable, so it stays chainable.

entries.name: align
entries.sig: (other: AlignTarget, pivot?: string | PointLike, alignment?: string | PointLike): this
entries.doc:
Translate this shape so that the `pivot` point on its own bbox coincides with
the `alignment` point on `other`'s bbox.

Both `pivot` and `alignment` accept:
- A keyword string combining any of: left, right, front, back, top, bottom
  (unspecified axes default to the centre of that axis)
- A PointLike [x%, y%, z%] where 0 = min-side and 1 = max-side

`other` may be a Shape, a Point, or a raw PointLike; a point is treated as a
zero-size bbox at that location (as if it were a Vertex).
examples:
box.align(shelf, 'bottom', 'top')  // sits box on top of shelf
box.align(other, 'center', 'center') // centres box on other
box.align(curve.middle(), 'lefttop') // align to a bare point

entries.name: alignByPoints
entries.sig: (sourcePoints: [PointLike, PointLike] | [PointLike, PointLike, PointLike], targetPoints: [PointLike, PointLike] | [PointLike, PointLike, PointLike], withScale?: boolean): this
entries.doc:
Align this Mesh by mapping 3 source points onto 3 target points.

- **withScale:** if true, apply a uniform scale (centered at q1) so edge lengths match.

params.name: sourcePoints
params.doc: 2 or 3 reference points on the mesh (current space)

params.name: targetPoints
params.doc: 2 or 3 corresponding destination points

params.name: withScale
params.doc: optionally scale uniformly to match first-edge length

entries.name: alignTo
entries.sig: (other: AlignTarget, pivot?: string | PointLike, alignment?: string | PointLike): this
entries.doc: Alias for align()

entries.name: annotations
entries.doc: Annotations linked to this Shape

entries.name: area
entries.doc: Surface area — sum of all polygon face areas

entries.name: array
entries.doc: Arrange copies of this Mesh in a 3-D array.
entries.returnsDoc: ShapeCollection<Mesh> containing all copies (the original sits at [0,0,0]).

params.name: sizes
params.doc:
Number of copies along [x, y, z] axes (default [2, 2, 1]).
Non-integer values are floored; values < 1 map to 1.

params.name: offsets
params.doc:
Distance between copy origins along [x, y, z].
Defaults to the bbox extent on each axis so copies are placed adjacent.

entries.name: autoDim
entries.sig: (options?: { offset?: number; offsetVec?: unknown; ortho?: boolean | "x" | "y" | "z"; roundDecimals?: number; showUnits?: boolean; units?: "mm" | "cm" | "dm" | "m" | "km" | "inch" | "feet" | "yd" | "mi" }, strategy?: string): any
entries.doc:
Automatic dimensioning of this shape (Annotator). `dim()` routes here by itself
for shapes a single bbox dimension cannot describe.

params.name: options
params.type: { offset?: number; offsetVec?: unknown; ortho?: boolean | "x" | "y" | "z"; roundDecimals?: number; showUnits?: boolean; units?: "mm" | "cm" | "dm" | "m" | "km" | "inch" | "feet" | "yd" | "mi" }

entries.name: autoRotate
entries.doc:
Rotate this Mesh to align as much as possible to the world axes.
Alias for rotateToOrtho()

entries.name: bbox
entries.doc:
Calculate outer bounding box of current Mesh.
The optional arg is ignored — kept for old-API compatibility.

entries.name: carbon
entries.doc: Embodied carbon (kgCO2e) of this shape. Defaults to cradle-to-gate A1-A3.

entries.name: center
entries.doc: Center of mass

entries.name: closestPoint
entries.sig: (x: number, y: number, z: number): ClosestPointResult
entries.doc: Project a query point onto the nearest mesh surface (BVH-accelerated).
entries.returnsDoc: Closest-point result, or `null` if the mesh is empty.

entries.name: color
entries.sig: (color: string | number, g?: number, b?: number): this

entries.name: copy
entries.doc:
Public copy. Clones via `_copy()`, then — unless this shape is `tmp()` — adds the
clone to the active layer. `copy()` means "give me a new shape", and new shapes render:
the clone is attached whenever a layer is reachable, which includes copying a DETACHED
but scene-derived shape (`curve.segments().first().copy()`) via the carried `_scene`.
The clone inherits the opaque `_modeler` and is flagged `_nameInherited` so the host
auto-namer can rename it after its variable.

Inside kernel operations use `_copy()` instead — it is the pure clone and never touches
the scene. Do NOT reach for `tmp()` there: `_suppressScene` is sticky and propagates to
every derived shape, so a tmp'd internal copy would suppress the real result too.

entries.name: cutoff
entries.sig: (at: Axis, coord?: number, smallest?: boolean): this
entries.doc:
Cut off Mesh by an axis-aligned plane at `coord` and keep one piece.
Keeps the larger piece by default (by size()); the smaller piece when `smallest=true`.
For a symmetric cut the positive-normal side is kept by default. Uses boolean
subtraction of half-space boxes rather than a mesh split.

entries.name: cutoffBy
entries.sig: (other: Mesh | Polygon | PlaneJs, keepSmallest?: boolean): this
entries.doc:
Cut this mesh by `other` and keep one of the resulting pieces.
By default keeps the largest piece (by size()); set `keepSmallest=true` to keep the
smallest. Cutting is done with boolean ops rather than a split: a Mesh/Polygon cutter
yields the outside piece (this − cutter) and the inside piece (this ∩ cutter); a PlaneJs
cutter yields the two half-spaces via boolean subtraction of a solid half-space box.

For Mesh and Polygon cutters, warns and returns `this` unchanged when `other`
does not intersect this mesh. PlaneJs cutters always proceed (planes are infinite).

entries.name: difference
entries.doc:
Subtract a Mesh — or every Mesh in a ShapeCollection — from the current.

Auto-separates: when the cut passes through and splits the solid into genuinely-separate
parts, the original is replaced in the scene by one Mesh per part and a ShapeCollection is
returned. A cut that only hollows out the solid (an internal cavity) is cavity-aware and
kept as a single Mesh. See separateIsolated.

entries.name: dim
entries.sig: (options?: { offset?: number; offsetVec?: unknown; ortho?: boolean | "x" | "y" | "z"; roundDecimals?: number; showUnits?: boolean; units?: "mm" | "cm" | "dm" | "m" | "km" | "inch" | "feet" | "yd" | "mi" }): any
entries.doc: Alias for dimension().

params.name: options
params.type: { offset?: number; offsetVec?: unknown; ortho?: boolean | "x" | "y" | "z"; roundDecimals?: number; showUnits?: boolean; units?: "mm" | "cm" | "dm" | "m" | "km" | "inch" | "feet" | "yd" | "mi" }

entries.name: dimension
entries.sig: (options?: { offset?: number; offsetVec?: unknown; ortho?: boolean | "x" | "y" | "z"; roundDecimals?: number; showUnits?: boolean; units?: "mm" | "cm" | "dm" | "m" | "km" | "inch" | "feet" | "yd" | "mi" }): any
entries.doc: Create dimension line(s) for this shape (Annotator).

params.name: options
params.type: { offset?: number; offsetVec?: unknown; ortho?: boolean | "x" | "y" | "z"; roundDecimals?: number; showUnits?: boolean; units?: "mm" | "cm" | "dm" | "m" | "km" | "inch" | "feet" | "yd" | "mi" }

entries.name: dispose
entries.doc:
Manual empty Csgrs reference 
NOTE: Only use if to quickly want to clear memory
Garbage collection should do this automatically (after some time)

entries.name: distance
entries.sig: (other: Point | Vertex | Mesh | Curve | Polygon): number
entries.doc: Alias for distanceTo

entries.name: distanceTo
entries.sig: (other: Point | Vertex | Mesh | Curve | Polygon): number
entries.doc:
Minimum separating distance to another Mesh, Curve, Point, Vertex, or Polygon.
For Curves the curve is tessellated and the minimum closestPoint distance
across all samples is returned. Returns `0` if they intersect.
For Points the distance is measured from the point position to the
closest point on the mesh surface.
For Vertices the distance is measured from the vertex position to the
closest point on the mesh surface.
For Polygons the polygon is converted to a mesh first.

entries.name: distanceToLegacy
entries.doc: Legacy uncached mesh-to-mesh distance path for side-by-side comparisons.

entries.name: distanceToPlane
entries.sig: (planeOrigin: [number, number, number], planeNormal: [number, number, number]): number
entries.doc: Minimum absolute distance from any vertex to a plane.

entries.name: edges
entries.doc:
The edges of this mesh as Curves, each unique edge returned once.

Derived from the face rings: every consecutive vertex pair of every polygon
(outer boundary and holes) is an edge, deduplicated by position. Endpoints are
quantised to a 1e-6 grid before keying, mirroring the kernel's own edge
extraction, so the two faces meeting at an edge agree on it.

The result is grouped by how many faces meet at the edge and how sharply:
  - 'boundary' — exactly one adjacent face (a naked/open edge)
  - 'crease'   — two faces meeting at more than `featureAngle` degrees
  - 'flat'     — two near-coplanar faces (usually a triangulation diagonal)

params.name: featureAngle
params.doc:
Dihedral angle in degrees above which an edge counts as a
crease. Default 10, matching the projection pipeline.

params.name: all
params.doc:
Return every edge including 'flat' ones. By default flat
edges are left out, since they are triangulation artefacts
rather than model edges. Call reconstructNgons() first to
remove most of them at the source.

entries.name: elevation
entries.sig: (from?: PointLike | BasePlane, method?: HlrStrategy, options?: ProjectionOptions): ShapeCollection<Shape>
alt: (from?: PointLike | BasePlane, hiddenLines?: boolean, samples?: number, featureAngle?: number, view?: ProjectionViewOptions): ShapeCollection<Shape>
entries.doc:
Orthographic elevation projection with hidden-line removal.

Renders the mesh as seen from `from`, projected onto the plane through
the origin perpendicular to `from`. Same pipeline as isometry
but with a domain-friendly direction argument (BasePlane name or Vector).
entries.returnsDoc:
ShapeCollection with groups 'visible', 'silhouette' (outer
contour, subset of 'visible'), and 'hidden' (only if requested).

params.name: from
params.doc:
Camera-side direction. Either a `BasePlane` name
('front', 'back', 'left', 'right', 'top', 'bottom',
'xy', 'xz', 'yz') or a `PointLike` direction.

params.name: method
params.doc:
Which hidden-line algorithm to run. Defaults to `'exact'`; the
per-shape methods `'clip'` and `'painter'` reduce to `'exact'` on a single mesh.

params.name: options
params.doc:
Projection settings — see ProjectionOptions.
`includeHiddenShapes` and `fallback` have nothing to act on for a single mesh.

entries.name: extrude
entries.doc:
Sweep this mesh along a direction to make a solid — the last step of the classic
vertex → line → face → solid chain, here for a *surface* built from several faces
(a lofted roof, a folded plate).

The solid is built directly: this surface is the bottom cap, a translated copy the top
cap, and every boundary edge is swept into a side wall. That keeps a folded surface (two
roof planes meeting at a ridge) as one watertight solid without any boolean work.
entries.returnsDoc: A new solid Mesh, or null when there is nothing to sweep.

params.name: length
params.doc: Distance to sweep.

params.name: direction
params.doc: Direction to sweep in. Defaults to +Z.

entries.name: faces
entries.doc: Get faces of the Mesh as a ShapeCollection of Polygons (alias of polygons())

entries.name: first
entries.doc:
The first shape of a single Shape is the Shape itself.

Ops that MAY split — `cutoffBy()`, `difference()`, `intersections()` — answer with one
Shape or with a ShapeCollection depending on the geometry, and a script cannot know which
in advance. `first()` lets the same line read either: `post.cutoffBy(diagonal).first()`.
brep's Shape carries the same method for the same reason.

entries.name: flatten
entries.doc:
Flatten this Mesh onto a coordinate plane: keep the polygons whose normal is
parallel to `axis`, collapse them onto the plane through the origin perpendicular
to that axis, and drop the doubles that creates.

Flattening a box along 'z' selects its top and bottom face; both land on the same
rectangle, so only one is kept — the same single-face result the brep kernel's
Solid.flatten() gives.

params.name: axis
params.doc:
Axis whose faces to keep and along which to collapse ('x' | 'y' | 'z',
default 'z' — the horizontal faces, flattened onto the XY plane).

entries.name: grid
entries.sig: (cx?: number, cy?: number, cz?: number, spacing?: PointLike): ShapeCollection<Mesh>
entries.doc:
Arrange copies of this Mesh on a 3-D grid.
Counts are floored and clamped to at least 1, so `grid(4, 3, 0)` is a flat 4x3 grid
in XY rather than an empty collection.
entries.returnsDoc:
ShapeCollection<Mesh> of all copies - this Mesh itself is the copy at
cell [0,0,0] (like row()), so the scene never gets a duplicate on top of it.

params.name: spacing
params.doc: Distance between copy origins, uniform or per axis.

entries.name: hits
entries.doc: Test whether this mesh physically overlaps another (BVH-accelerated).

entries.name: hull
entries.doc: Return new Mesh that is convex hull of current Mesh

entries.name: intersect
entries.doc:
Keep only the volume this Mesh shares with another (boolean AND), replacing this Mesh by
it — the mutating counterpart of intersection(), spelled the way union() and difference()
are (and the way brep's intersect() is).

entries.name: intersection
entries.doc:
The volume this Mesh shares with another (boolean AND).

NON-REPLACING: this Mesh is left exactly as it is; the shared volume comes back as a NEW
Mesh that is added to the active layer, so it is visible without an explicit
addToScene(). Mark this Mesh tmp() to keep the result out of the scene.

entries.name: intersectionPointsCurve
entries.doc:
Find intersection points between a Curve and this Mesh.
The curve is tessellated into a polyline and each segment is tested
against every triangle of the mesh surface.
entries.returnsDoc: Array of intersection Points, in order along the curve. Empty array if none found.

params.name: curve
params.doc: A Curve instance (NurbsCurve or CompoundCurve)

params.name: tolerance
params.doc: Tessellation tolerance for the curve (default: 1e-4)

entries.name: intersects
entries.doc:
Alias for hits(): do these two meshes physically overlap?
More stable than comparing distances when you only need a yes/no.

entries.name: inverse
entries.doc: Flip all polygon normals (reverses winding order)

entries.name: is2D
entries.doc: Whether this mesh's bounding box has zero extent on one axis

entries.name: is3D
entries.doc:
Whether this Shape has extent along all three axes — the complement of is2D(), which
Mesh and Curve each define from their bbox. Kept on the base class because callers
outside meshup (the host annotator deciding which way to offset a dimension line) ask
any Shape, and a missing method there is a crash, not a `false`.

entries.name: isCuboid
entries.doc:
Whether this Mesh is essentially a cuboid (box / rectangular plate).

Builds the PCA-based OBB and checks every unique vertex against the box
surface in OBB-local coords: each vertex must lie within ±halfExtent on
every non-zero axis AND touch (within `tolerance`) at least one face
along a non-zero axis. Tessellated boxes (mid-edge / face-centre verts)
still pass; curved surfaces do not.

is2D() is not enough on its own: it is also true for a mesh standing up in Z (a wall),
which drawn from above collapses to a single line.

methods `'clip'` and `'painter'` reduce to `'exact'` here.

mesh has no hidden shapes to filter and no per-shape method to fall back

entries.name: layflat
entries.doc:
Rotate the mesh to lay flat on the XY plane, then drop it so its bottom sits at Z = 0.
Aligns the dominant face direction — the normal carrying the largest total face area —
with world Z, along the shortest arc, so the in-plane orientation is never disturbed.
A mesh whose dominant face is already parallel to XY is therefore only translated.

NOT the OBB's thinnest axis: that is a PCA direction of least variance and only lines
up with a real face on plate-like shapes. On a sheared loft or a blocky part it points
nowhere near a face, and layflat() would leave the shape tilted with nothing at all
resting on Z = 0. Going by face area is also what keeps degenerate plates (equal X/Y
eigenvalues, arbitrary eigenvectors) stable — their two big faces group together
regardless of how the PCA in-plane axes happen to fall.

That is the difference between this and setting the properties back to

entries.doc:

The quaternion is normalized internally, so non-unit input is safe.
NOTE: We guarantee the center is always to origin one

params.name: wOrObj

entries.doc: Rotate so `fromDir` maps to `toDir`, with no roll (up stays stable).

params.name: up
params.doc: The world direction that should remain as "upright" as possible after rotation (default [0,0,1]).

entries.name: rotateToAlignLargestFaceToZ
entries.doc:
Rotate this Mesh so the normal of its dominant face direction is parallel to the Z axis.

Faces are grouped by normal (opposite normals count as one direction) and the group
with the largest *total* area wins. Grouping matters here: a tessellated mesh has its
faces split into many triangles, so the single largest polygon is a poor proxy for the
face that actually dominates the shape.

entries.name: rotateToAxesOBbox
entries.doc:
Rotate this Mesh so its oriented bounding box lines up with the world axes:
the OBB's thinnest axis onto +Z first, then its longest axis onto +X.
Position of the center is kept.

entries.name: rotateToOrtho
entries.doc:
Rotate this Mesh to align it with the world axes as much as possible.

Runs in three steps:
  1. `rotateToAxesOBbox()` — get the shape roughly flat on the XY plane
  2. `rotateToAlignLargestFaceToZ()` — make the dominant face parallel to XY
  3. turn around Z so the dominant edge direction lands on the X or Y axis

Step 3 only ever turns around Z (by at most a quarter turn), so it can never
undo the flat alignment of the first two steps.

params.name: o
params.doc:
'vertical' (default) puts the dominant edge direction on the Y axis,
'horizontal' puts it on the X axis

entries.name: rotateVecToVec
entries.sig: (from: PointLike, to: PointLike, pivot?: PointLike): this
entries.doc:
Rotate this Mesh so that direction `from` ends up pointing along `to`, using the
shortest arc between the two.

params.name: pivot
params.doc: point the rotation turns around (default: this Mesh's center)

entries.name: row
entries.sig: (count: number, spacing?: number, direction?: PointLike | Axis): ShapeCollection<Mesh>
entries.doc:
Create a row of copies of this Mesh with specific spacing between them

Spacing is measured from the bounding boxes of the meshes, so they are placed adjacent plus the specified spacing.

params.name: count
params.doc: number of copies in the row (including the original)

params.name: spacing
params.doc: distance between bounding boxes of copies (default: 10)

params.name: direction
params.doc:
direction of the row (default: 'x')

NOTE: We don't use csgrs distribute_linear() because it merges meshes into one
    We want to output a collection of individual meshes

entries.name: sampleSDF
entries.sig: (x: number, y: number, z: number): SdfSample
entries.doc:
Sample the signed distance field at a query point.
Negative distance = inside the mesh.
entries.returnsDoc: SDF sample, or `null` if the mesh is empty.

entries.name: scale
entries.doc: Scale Mesh with a uniform factor or per-axis [sx, sy, sz] around an origin point (default: center of this Mesh)

entries.name: section
entries.sig: (pivot: PointLike, normal?: PointLike | BasePlane, method?: HlrStrategy, options?: ProjectionOptions): ShapeCollection<Shape>
alt: (pivot: PointLike, normal?: PointLike | BasePlane, hiddenLines?: boolean, samples?: number, featureAngle?: number, view?: ProjectionViewOptions): ShapeCollection<Shape>
entries.doc:
Architectural section: cut the mesh with a plane and project the
geometry beyond the cut onto that same plane with HLR.

The viewer looks along `-normal` (so for the default normal=[0,0,1]
the camera is above, looking down — the standard floor-plan setup).

The underlying csgrs `slice()` drops Z when building the cut
sketch; this works correctly for cuts whose normal has a
non-trivial Z component. Vertical sections (normal in XY
plane) currently produce a degenerate cut profile.
entries.returnsDoc:
ShapeCollection with groups 'cut', 'visible', 'silhouette'
(outer contour, subset of 'visible'), and 'hidden' (if requested).

params.name: pivot
params.doc: Any point on the section plane.

params.name: normal
params.doc:
Section plane normal (BasePlane name or PointLike).
Default `[0,0,1]` (horizontal cut).

params.name: method
params.doc:
Which hidden-line algorithm to run. Defaults to `'exact'`; the
per-shape methods `'clip'` and `'painter'` reduce to `'exact'` on a single mesh.

params.name: options
params.doc:
Projection settings — see ProjectionOptions.
`includeHiddenShapes` and `fallback` have nothing to act on for a single mesh.

entries.name: select
entries.doc:
Select (sub)shapes with a selector string (see Selector.ts).
Selectors are greedy: an underspecified selector returns every match.
A ShapeCollection result is collapsed to the single shape when there is
exactly one match (checkSingle), and an empty result warns.
Selecting does not add anything to the scene - it hands back a reference to
geometry that is already there. `select(…).copy()` is what puts a new shape in.

entries.name: selected
entries.doc: True when this shape is currently selected (clicked) in the viewer.

entries.name: separateIsolated
entries.doc:
Separate this Mesh into its genuinely-separate solid parts (e.g. after a subtract whose
cut passes through and splits the solid). Returns a ShapeCollection<Mesh> with one entry
per part; a solid that is still one piece returns a collection containing only this mesh.

Cavity-aware: connectivity is by shared surface vertices, so a solid with a fully-internal
cavity (a blind hole / void) has a disconnected inner shell — but that shell is spatially
contained within the outer shell, so it is recognised as a cavity and kept together with
its solid rather than split off. Only non-nested components are returned as separate parts.

Scene: when this mesh is in the scene and it does split into several parts, the original is
replaced by the parts on its layer; a still-single solid is left in place.

entries.name: setId
entries.doc:
Overwrite this shape's id. Ids are minted per construction, so a shape rebuilt from
a saved document would otherwise come back with a fresh uuid and lose every reference
to it (scene links, host selection, undo entries). Deserialisers call this to restore
identity; nothing else should.

entries.name: sid
entries.doc: Serial id: the order this shape entered the scene, or 0 if it never did. See `_sid`.

entries.name: size
entries.doc:
General size estimate: the solid volume when it is meaningfully positive, otherwise the
surface area. A flat (2D) mesh has zero volume, so callers that rank meshes by size (e.g.
cutoff()/cutoffBy()) get area as the right discriminator there instead of tying at 0.

entries.name: split
entries.doc:
Split this mesh into two pieces using a cutting `other`.

- `Mesh`    — the cutter volume is removed and the remaining isolated pieces are returned.
- `Polygon` — the polygon's plane is used as the cutting plane.
- `PlaneJs` — the plane is used directly (front side = direction the normal points).

Returns a `ShapeCollection<Mesh>` with one entry per remaining piece. For plane-based
splits this is typically up to two entries (front/positive side first, back/negative
side second). Empty results are omitted.

entries.name: strokeWidth
entries.doc:
Line width in SCREEN PIXELS — not model units.

It travels to the viewer as `BENTLEY_materials_line_style.width` and becomes a pixel
`linewidth` on the fat-line material, so a line keeps the same apparent weight however
far you zoom. `thickness(4)` is four pixels, not four millimetres.

entries.name: subtract
entries.doc:
Subtract one or more Meshes (or ShapeCollections) from the current. Like difference(),
a cut that splits the solid into genuinely-separate parts auto-separates into one Mesh per
part (returned as a ShapeCollection); an internal cavity is kept as a single Mesh.

entries.name: thickness
entries.doc: Alias for `strokeWidth()`. Reads more naturally for a curve. Screen pixels.

entries.name: tmp
entries.doc:
Mark this shape as temporary: detach it from the scene AND set a sticky
`_suppressScene` flag so that every subsequent scene op (copy/extrude/split/…) on it
is a no-op and every shape derived from it is `tmp()` too. Ideal for building helper
geometry inside advanced methods. `addToScene()` (host) clears the flag. Returns `this`.

entries.sig: (cssClass?: string, styleOpts?: { nonScalingStroke?: boolean; omitDefaults?: boolean }): string

Return the SVG elements for this Mesh's faces — one `<polygon>` (or `<path>`, for a
face with holes) each — without the outer `<svg>` wrapper. Used by ShapeCollection and
SceneNode to compose a drawing.

Faces are drawn from above, as Polygon.toSVGElem() draws them: exact for a mesh lying
on a plane parallel to XY (see isFlatOnXY()), a projection for anything else. Every
face is drawn with the MESH's style — the Polygon wrappers faces() hands out are fresh
each call and carry the default style, not the one the author set on the mesh.

Several elements, not a `<g>` wrapping them: the callers assemble flat element lists
and add the grouping (and the class) they need themselves.

entries.name: fromGLTF
entries.sig: (data: string | ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>, metadata?: any, up?: Axis): Mesh
entries.doc:
Import a glTF 2.0 model (.glb or .gltf) as a single merged Mesh.
Materials + node hierarchy are flattened.
Self-contained .glb / base64 .gltf only (no Draco / external buffers).

`up` is the up axis **inside the file**, and it mirrors Mesh.toGLTF's
parameter so that `Mesh.fromGLTF(await m.toGLB())` returns `m` unrotated:
 - `'z'` (default) — what meshup writes. The Archiyou stack carries the kernel's
   native Z-up through to a Z-up viewer, so those files hold Z-up coordinates.
 - `'y'` — a conforming glTF, i.e. anything Blender / three.js produced.

Nothing in a glTF distinguishes the two, so a file from elsewhere needs
`Mesh.fromGLTF(data, null, 'y')` or it arrives lying on its side.

entries.name: fromOBJ
entries.doc:
Import a Wavefront OBJ mesh from its text content.
NOTE: requires a WASM build that exposes MeshJs.fromOBJ (cast to any to
decouple from the generated csgrs.d.ts — see Importer).

entries.name: fromPointsWithHoles
entries.doc:
Create a Mesh from an outer boundary polygon with optional interior holes.
Each hole is an array of PointLike defining an interior boundary.
The polygon is triangulated (including proper hole subtraction) and returned as a Mesh.

entries.name: fromPolygons
entries.doc:
Create Mesh directly from planar polygons defined by (N >= 3) vertices
For some export formats (like STL) polygons are triangulated first

Only positions are given here, so every vertex would be born with a ZERO normal:
Point.toVertexJs() defaults to (0,0,0). That is not a cosmetic detail — a
zero-normal surface takes no light, so the mesh renders flat grey in any PBR
viewer however it is coloured (and exports a useless NORMAL buffer to glTF). Each
polygon therefore gets its own plane normal assigned to its vertices, i.e. these
meshes are flat-shaded. Callers that have real per-vertex normals (a tessellated
curved surface, say) should build their own PolygonJs with them — see
Point.toVertexJs(normal) — and go through Mesh.from(MeshJs.fromPolygons(...)).

rounding the coordinates themselves carry (a few ULP), and nothing can be authored,
measured or manufactured at that width. See _cutoffClosedByRegion().
